One or two claims per page; not an exhaustive reading. PRELIMINARY_RESEARCH; not owner approved.

claims.subject: sarkhan_vol

evidence.quote: Khanfall The dragons owe their oppressive victory to the Planeswalker Sarkhan Vol.
His actions saved the Planeswalker Ugin, the spirit dragon, from death at the hands of Nicol Bolas.

claims.summary: Sarkhan's time-travel intervention saved Ugin from death at Bolas's hands and led to the dragons' victory (the Khanfall timeline).

claims.subject: ugin

evidence.quote: Ugin was instead gravely injured but survived and entered a long hibernation inside a nest of hedrons on Tarkir.

claims.summary: Gravely injured, Ugin hibernated inside a nest of hedrons on Tarkir.

claims.subject: ugin

evidence.quote: As Ugin healed, his draconic essence mingled with the soul of the plane, further empowering the dragonstorms.
No longer empowered by his essence, the dragonstorms finally lessened.

claims.summary: Ugin's essence, mingling with the plane as he healed, empowered the dragonstorms; they lessened after he left.

claims.subject: ugin

evidence.quote: Five years ago, Ugin awoke from his hibernation and departed Tarkir.

claims.summary: Ugin awoke and departed Tarkir five years before the Dragonstorm story.
claims.limitation: 'Five years ago' is relative to the guide's present (2025 release).

claims.subject: dragonlords

evidence.quote: Led by the powerful dragonlords, the dragons' forces were ultimately able to hunt down and kill the clan leaders and decimate their numbers.

claims.summary: In the Khanfall timeline the dragonlords' forces killed the clan leaders and ruled Tarkir.

claims.subject: narset

evidence.quote: Narset and the other rebellion leaders gathered at the remains of the Crucible of the Spirit Dragon, hoping to finally put an end to the dragonlords' reign.
The former Planeswalker Narset hoped to find a way to end what she saw as a perpetual battle of attrition that would leave Tarkir as little more than ruins.

claims.summary: The former Planeswalker Narset was one of the rebellion leaders who gathered at the Crucible of the Spirit Dragon to end the dragonlords' reign.

claims.subject: sultai

evidence.quote: Living in the jungles of Tarkir, the Sultai are adept at transforming challenge into opportunity.
In the Sultai, not even death can stop the most valuable members of the clan, as their powerful necromancers raise their honored dead to continue to lead and serve.

claims.summary: The Sultai live in Tarkir's jungles; their necromancers raise honored dead to keep leading and serving.

claims.subject: mardu

evidence.quote: The Mardu claim the central steppes and grassy plains of Tarkir as their territory, assembling massive mobile cities as they traverse the landscape.

claims.summary: The nomadic Mardu claim Tarkir's central steppes and plains, moving in massive mobile cities.

claims.subject: mehtma

evidence.quote: Three were krumar, orphans adopted into House Fenzala as Mehtma herself had been.

claims.summary: Mehtma, a lieutenant, was a krumar orphan adopted into the Abzan House Fenzala.

claims.subject: narset

evidence.quote: Although Narset was the waymaster—the actual leader of the Jeskai now, really, to her periodic chagrin—so it seemed equally possible they'd see her attention as a boon.

claims.summary: Narset is the Jeskai waymaster, effectively the clan's leader.

claims.subject: elspeth_tirel

evidence.quote: Elspeth took absent note of the fact no one else on the skyship had come to interrogate her about her presence, not after she explained to a flustered dignitary that she was here to see Narset, please, and was cordially told to make herself at home until the waymaster could be retrieved.

claims.summary: Elspeth, now winged, comes to a Jeskai skyship to see Narset.

claims.subject: cori_mountain_monastery

evidence.quote: Only one of us is now an esteemed monk of the Cori Mountain Monastery, after all."
I'm an embarrassment to my fellow disciples, and I dragged the Jeskai name through the dirt."

claims.summary: The Cori Mountain Monastery trains Jeskai disciples and monks.
claims.limitation: Affiliation is inferred from dialogue; the narrator is not named in these lines.

claims.subject: ajani

evidence.quote: On some level, Ajani had hoped that if he did enough good, it would expunge from his soul all the sins he committed while he was Elesh Norn's slavish little pet.

claims.summary: Ajani, now living alone in Tarkir's wilderness, seeks atonement for the sins he committed while serving Elesh Norn.
claims.limitation: Past service while compleated; the phrasing is Ajani's own self-judgment.

claims.subject: titsui

evidence.quote: Me and Titsui, my second-in-command … we would … our army and us … every fortnight or so … every week maybe … we would march into a new territory, a town or a village, and claim it as our own.

claims.summary: Nishang, a dying Sultai veteran, names Titsui as his former second-in-command.
claims.limitation: Told by Nishang in a drunken boast; the story itself undercuts his account.

claims.subject: taigam

evidence.quote: The monk Taigam had named himself as a loyalist, but there was something in his expressions and speech that suggested to Sarkhan zealot might have been a better description.
"This is how you fly with a dragon's wings once more," said Taigam, as though he had somehow heard Sarkhan's hesitation.

claims.summary: The loyalist monk Taigam leads Sarkhan to hunt a dragon and take its heart to regain his dragon form.

claims.subject: paala

evidence.quote: Moreover, her first dragonstorm had heralded such a change that it had scorched her heart, leaving lightning scars where no one could see them.

claims.summary: Paala, a Mardu girl, was changed and scarred by her first dragonstorm.
claims.limitation: The nature of the change is revealed later in the story and is not graded here.

claims.subject: felothar

evidence.quote: The problem with the new khan of the Abzan, Ajani thought, wasn't the fact that she was a soldier at heart, but that she had no illusions about this.
As a result, Felothar often spent ages deliberating on matters with the help of her Council of Houses; each of the house representatives' opinions were given equal weight and consideration.

claims.summary: Felothar is the new khan of the Abzan and governs with a Council of Houses.

claims.subject: ajani

evidence.quote: He could not bear to look at Elspeth, his last words to her still echoing in his memories.
Worse, still, he had wanted to kill her.

claims.summary: Ajani remembers that, while compleated, he tried and wanted to kill Elspeth.
claims.limitation: Refers back to their fight during the New Phyrexia arc.

claims.subject: ureni

evidence.quote: Azure wraps around the people of the Temur as they sleep, leaping from one family to the next, binding wrists and throats and tongues.
Anyone else would be trembling in fear, but Ureni knows it is anger driving her now, a fiery need to protect.

claims.summary: The dragon Ureni tries to protect the Temur from blue threads that bind and kill them.
claims.limitation: Ureni's species and role are given poetically; 'protected' is IMPLIED. The story uses both 'they' and 'her' for Ureni.

claims.subject: vraska

evidence.quote: Without a spark, Vraska and Loot had to travel by Omenpaths, and Jace was forced to traverse the Multiverse without the ease a Planeswalker was accustomed to.

claims.summary: Sparkless, Vraska travels with Jace and Loot through the Omenpaths.
claims.limitation: Set 'Some Time Ago' relative to the main Dragonstorm episodes.

claims.subject: jace_beleren

evidence.quote: They knew which Omenpaths would ultimately lead them to Tarkir, and from Tarkir to the Meditation Realm, thanks to Loot.

claims.summary: Thanks to Loot, Jace and Vraska know the Omenpath route to Tarkir and from there to the Meditation Realm.
claims.limitation: That the Meditation Realm is Jace's goal is inferred from this route.

claims.subject: sarkhan_vol

evidence.quote: The ritual had done something to the dragonstorms, something to him, too: Sarkhan had expected his transformation, but not this control over the dragons themselves.
More dragons emerged from the clouds, and in their eyes, Sarkhan saw reverence.

claims.summary: After the ritual, the transformed Sarkhan finds he can control Tarkir's dragons.
claims.limitation: The quote says 'the dragons', not the dragonlords specifically; the object is the closest existing faction.

remaining: Every TDM page is cited with one to three claims; the ritual at the Crucible, Sarkhan's betrayal and the episode climaxes are only lightly modelled
The Abzan, Jeskai and Temur guide sections are not graded beyond one claim each
Ureni's identity (and their link to Ugin) is not graded
